Daily Life

Living in Chofu

Daily life in Chofu: grocery shopping, garbage sorting, and everything in between.

Transport

Getting Around

Keio Line

Chofu Station is on the Keio Line. Direct trains to Shinjuku (20 min, express). Also connects to Kichijoji, Meiji-jingumae, and Shinjuku Sanchome.

~300 yen to Shinjuku · IC card accepted

Buses

Chofu City runs local buses connecting residential areas to the station. Use Google Maps for routes. The "Chofu City Mini Bus" covers key spots including UEC.

~200 yen per ride · IC card accepted

Bicycles

Bicycles are the most popular way to get around. You must register your bike with Chofu City (anti-theft law). Buy a used bike at Hard-Off for 5,000–10,000 yen.

Registration: ~500 yen · Park in designated areas

Daily Life

Everyday Essentials

♻️

Garbage Disposal

Chofu requires designated bags. Buy them at convenience stores or supermarkets:

  • Red: Burnable waste (kitchen scraps, paper)
  • Blue: Non-burnable (plastics, metals)
  • Transparent: Recyclable plastics

Pickup schedule varies by area. Check your building's notice board.

📦

Mail & Packages

Your mailbox will have your name in Japanese. For Amazon packages, use the delivery box or receive at your door. If not home, a delivery slip (fusen) will tell you where to pick up.

Amazon Japan delivers to Chofu in 1–2 days

📶

Internet Setup

UEC provides campus-wide Wi-Fi (UEC-Wireless). For your dorm/apartment, you'll need to sign up with an ISP. Popular options: NURO, AsahiNet, or pocket WiFi via Rakuten Mobile.

Setup takes 1–3 weeks · Start early
